label.purpose: Field name and row captions, uppercase, tracked.

numeric.purpose: Every amount input and computed monetary value, tabular numerals. The rate fields (Service Comm %, Our Comm %) use the same role at a smaller 18px size.

components.name: Card
components.description: The bordered black console holding the whole calculator.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #000000; color: #ffffff; border: 3px solid #ffffff; border-radius: 0; padding: 24px; }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: USD / AED / Received Amount fields — large tabular numerals, hard white border, all three fully bidirectionally linked, comma-grouped as you type.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; font-size: 28px; font-weight: 800; padding: 12px 14px; border-radius: 0; border: 2px solid #ffffff; background: #000000; color: #ffffff; outline: none; caret-color: #87a96b; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #999999; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #87a96b; outline: 2px solid #87a96b; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Rate Field
components.description: Service Comm % / Our Comm % — the same input at a smaller scale, two placed side by side since they are peers, not a sequence.
components.css: .ds-rate-input { width: 100%; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 800; padding: 10px 10px 10px 26px; border-radius: 0; border: 2px solid #ffffff; background: #000000; color: #ffffff; outline: none; caret-color: #87a96b; } .ds-rate-input:focus { border-color: #87a96b; outline: 2px solid #87a96b; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Nested Breakdown Row
components.description: Wraps a figure that is mathematically a component of the row above it (Service Comm is a child of Comm Main; Our Comm is too but is promoted out into its own headline block) — a left rule and indent make the parent/child relationship visible without a label.
components.css: .ds-nested { border-left: 2px solid #ffffff; padding-left: 14px; } .ds-row { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; font-size: 14px; } .ds-row-label { color: #999999; } .ds-row-val { color: #ffffff; font-weight: 700; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Our Comm Block
components.description: The headline total — the owner's own earnings, the page's one filled surface, in calm Sage. Marks ownership, not magnitude: Received Amount and Comm Main are both larger figures and stay unaccented.
components.css: .ds-total { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; background: #87a96b; border: 2px solid #000000; padding: 14px 16px; } .ds-total-label { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 1.5px; text-transform: uppercase; color: #000000; } .ds-total-val { font-size: 28px; font-weight: 900; color: #000000; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

narrative.overview: Everything here reads like a clean instrument panel: black field, crisp white rules, tracked uppercase labels, and exactly one calm accent reserved for the number that matters. There's no ornament and no rounded softness, but the tone is measured rather than urgent — a quiet readout, not a warning light. Weight does the talking: nothing on screen is drawn lighter than 700, so even the smallest label stays clear and legible without needing to shout.
keyCharacteristics: Void-black field with crisp white 2-3px rules standing in for all depth and separation
Exactly one calm accent color (Sage), spent only on Our Comm, the owner's own earnings
All type at 700-900 weight; uppercase, tracked labels; tabular numerals throughout
Zero border-radius everywhere — every shape is a clean rectangle
No shadows at all — the border alone defines the card; function over form
Information is drawn as a real tree: Received Amount and Comm Main are siblings derived from AED; Service Comm nests under Comm Main because it is defined as part of its sum

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent color appears in exactly one place: Our Comm, the owner's own earnings. Everywhere else — including Received Amount and Comm Main, both larger dollar figures — stays black, white, or gray, so when the accent shows up it simply marks "this is the number that's actually yours," calmly rather than urgently.

rules.name: The No Regular Weight Rule
rules.body: Nothing on this screen is drawn below font-weight 700 — thin or regular type stays out of this system, keeping labels legible without any of them needing to be loud about it.

rules.name: The No Decoration Rule
rules.body: A border defines a boundary; it does not also need a shadow to prove it. If a visual device isn't load-bearing for reading the numbers, it doesn't ship.

rules.name: The Shape-Is-The-Math Rule
rules.body: A value that is derived as the sum of two other values is drawn nested under them, connected by a rule. Flattening a parent/child relationship into a plain list is a layout bug, not a style choice. Exception: the One Accent Rule outranks this one for exactly one row — Our Comm is mathematically Comm Main's child, but is promoted out of the nest into its own block because it's the headline number. A promotion needs the One Accent Rule's justification; it is not a second precedent for un-nesting anything else.

dos: Do keep the accent confined to the Our Comm block — the One Accent Rule.
Do keep every border and rule hard-edged (0px radius) and at least 2px thick.
Do keep text weight at 700+ everywhere; no thin or regular type.
Do draw a derived value nested under the values it's derived from — the Shape-Is-The-Math Rule.
donts: Don't add any shadow, soft or hard — the border alone defines the card; depth cues are decoration this system doesn't spend on.
Don't load an external webfont; the app must render and cache fully offline.
Don't give Comm Main its own independently-editable rate — it must always equal Service Comm + Our Comm exactly, per PRODUCT.md's calculation model.
Don't reach for an urgent or alarm-style color for the accent — the whole point of this palette is that the one signal color reads as calm, not urgent.
